Such a section is therefore unique, and exists if and only if the marked object of \(F(X)\) is invariant under \(\pi_F\). Finally, an object of a Galois category is said to be completely decomposed if it is isomorphic to a sum of final objects, i.e. if \(\pi_F\) operates trivially on \(F(X)\) — a condition obviously stronger than the existence of a pointed section, when \(X\) is pointed. Proposition 4 follows trivially from the preceding definitions and remarks.

proposals.before: Here (after Serre) is a simple way to realize the conditions of this example, taking inspiration from [5]: one takes for \(n\) a prime number \(\geqslant 5\), distinct from the characteristic, and one makes \(G=\mathbf{Z}/n\mathbf{Z}\) act on \(\underline{k}^4\)2 by multiplying the coordinates by four distinct characters of \(G\) (which is possible since \(n\geqslant 5\)). Then \(G\) acts on the projective space \(\mathbf{P}^3_k\), and the only fixed points under \(G\) are the four points corresponding to the coordinate axes. The surface \(X'\) of equation \(x^n+y^n+z^n+t^n=0\) is smooth over \(k\) (Jacobian criterion), and contains none of the fixed points, so \(G\), being of prime order, acts on \(X\) “without fixed points”, i.e. \(X\) is a principal covering of \(X=X'/G\) with group \(G\). Let \(g=x/y\) in \(k(X')=K'\); it is a Kummer generator of \(K'\) over \(K=k(X)\) if the chosen characters were \(\chi^i\), \(i=0,1,2,3\), with \(\chi\) a primitive character, let \(f\) be its \(n\)-th power, which is an element of \(K\). One sees at once that \(K'\) is a regular extension of \(k(g)\), which results from the fact that the plane curve of homogeneous equation in \(U,T,Z\): \(T^n+Z^n+(1+g^n)U^n=0\) is smooth over \(k(g)\) (Jacobian criterion), and that one knows that every plane curve is connected. On the other hand one has \(k(f)=K\cap k(g)\), since the right-hand side is an extension of \(k(f)\) contained in the extension \(k(g)\) of prime degree, and distinct from \(k(g)\) (since \(g\not\in K\)). This implies that \(K\) is a regular extension of \(k(f)\). Finally the divisor of \(f\) on \(X\) is an \(n\)-th multiple of a divisor, for its inverse image on \(X'\) is the divisor of \(g^n\), hence an \(n\)-th multiple, and one can descend because \(X'\) is étale over \(X\). One would be done if the rational map \(f\colon X\mathchoice{\longrightarrow}{\rightarrow}{\rightarrow}{\rightarrow} \mathbf{P}^1\) were a morphism, that is to say if the divisors of the zeros and of the poles of \(f\) did not meet. In fact, one verifies easily (by looking again on \(X'\)) that the two divisors in question are the products by \(n\) of two curves smooth over \(k\), meeting transversally at a point \(a\). Replacing now \(X\) by the scheme obtained by blowing up \(a\), the preceding conditions (\(\operatorname{div}(f)\) divisible by \(n\), and \(k(X_1)=k(X)\) a regular extension of \(k(X)\)) remain satisfied, but moreover \(f\) is a morphism \(X_1\mathchoice{\longrightarrow}{\rightarrow}{\rightarrow}{\rightarrow} \mathbf{P}^1\), so we are under the desired conditions.

\[ \mathrm{H}^0(X,F)\mathchoice{\longrightarrow}{\rightarrow}{\rightarrow}{\rightarrow}\mathrm{H}^0(X_t,F|X_t)=1 \]

\[ g^* f_* F \mathchoice{\longrightarrow}{\rightarrow}{\rightarrow}{\rightarrow} f'_* F' \]

est fidèle (resp. pleinement fidèle, resp. une équivalence de catégories).
